ingredients.name: Vinpocetine

safety_hits.reason: Vinpocetine is a synthetic derivative of the alkaloid vincamine, used as a prescription drug in Europe and Japan. In 2019 FDA issued a statement concluding that vinpocetine does not qualify as a dietary ingredient and cannot lawfully be included in dietary supplements — it was investigated as a drug before any supplement marketing. FDA additionally flagged potential fetal harm: animal studies showed decreased fetal weight and miscarriage, prompting the agency to warn that pregnant women and women of childbearing age should avoid it.

ingredients.name: Ginkgo (Ginkgo biloba) extract
ingredients.notes: Gold-standard ginkgo extract standardized to 24% flavone glycosides and 6% terpene lactones. Absolute oral bioavailability: ginkgolide A 80%, ginkgolide B 88%, bilobalide 79% (PMID:7631288, Fourtillan 1995 IV reference). Flavone glycosides extensively conjugated (low free form). EGb 761 is the most-studied branded version with strong evidence for cerebral blood flow and cognitive function.

condition_hits.mechanism: Ginkgo biloba increases hepatic CYP450 activity, accelerating metabolism of calcium channel blockers (nicardipine studied) and reducing their antihypertensive effect.
condition_hits.action: Inform prescriber. Blood pressure may be less well-controlled. Dose adjustment may be needed.
condition_hits.alert_body: Ginkgo may affect drug metabolism and could change effects of some blood pressure medicines. If you take BP medication, review ginkgo use with your clinician.
condition_hits.informational_note: Ginkgo can affect blood pressure — relevant to people with high blood pressure.

condition_hits.mechanism: Ginkgo biloba seeds and insufficiently processed leaf products contain ginkgotoxin (4-O-methylpyridoxine), which inhibits GABA synthesis by depleting pyridoxal-5-phosphate cofactor, producing proconvulsant effects. Standardized 24% flavonoid / 6% terpene leaf extracts with ginkgotoxin removed are lower risk, but purity cannot be guaranteed from all manufacturers.
condition_hits.action: Use ginkgo with caution or avoid in seizure disorders. Use only standardized ginkgo leaf extract from reputable manufacturers. Monitor for increased seizure frequency.
condition_hits.alert_body: Ginkgo seed and some products can contain ginkgotoxin, which may provoke seizures. If you have epilepsy or take antiseizure medication, review ginkgo use with your clinician.
condition_hits.informational_note: Ginkgo may affect seizure threshold — relevant to people with a seizure disorder.

condition_hits.mechanism: Ginkgolides (especially ginkgolide B) inhibit platelet-activating factor (PAF), reducing platelet aggregation and extending bleeding time. Multiple case reports of spontaneous hemorrhage including subdural hematoma.
condition_hits.action: Avoid ginkgo with bleeding disorders. If used, monitor for bruising, prolonged bleeding, or unexplained headache.
condition_hits.alert_body: Ginkgo inhibits platelet-activating factor and has been linked to bleeding events in case reports. If you have a bleeding disorder, avoid unless your clinician specifically recommends it.
condition_hits.informational_note: Ginkgo affects platelet function — relevant to people with bleeding disorders.

condition_hits.mechanism: PAF inhibition by ginkgolides increases perioperative bleeding risk. Discontinue at least 2 weeks before scheduled surgery.
condition_hits.action: Discontinue ginkgo at least 14 days before surgery.
condition_hits.alert_headline: Ginkgo may increase surgical bleeding risk
condition_hits.alert_body: If you have surgery scheduled, stop ginkgo at least 2 weeks before unless your surgical team advises otherwise. It may increase perioperative bleeding.
condition_hits.informational_note: Ginkgo affects platelet function — relevant to anyone preparing for surgery.

condition_hits.mechanism: Antiplatelet activity raises bleeding-risk concerns in pregnancy and labor.
condition_hits.action: Use caution in pregnancy due to bleeding-risk profile, especially around delivery.
condition_hits.alert_body: There isn't enough specific safety data to give a confident recommendation for pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your obstetrician or pediatrician before using this supplement.
condition_hits.informational_note: Pregnancy/lactation safety data is limited — clinician guidance recommended.

inactive_ingredients.name: hypoallergenic Plant Fiber
inactive_ingredients.notes: MCC is the most widely used tablet excipient in the supplement and pharmaceutical industry. FDA GRAS with decades of safe use. EFSA and JECFA set no ADI limit. Low severity — tracked purely as non-nutritive filler quality signal.
inactive_ingredients.mechanism_of_harm: Inert, indigestible cellulose polymer used as tablet binder and filler. Passes through the GI tract unabsorbed. No evidence of systemic toxicity, nutrient absorption interference, or microbiome disruption at approved use levels. EFSA and JECFA set no ADI limit. Nanoparticle concerns are theoretical and unsubstantiated at food/supplement grades.
population_warnings: No specific population concerns at standard excipient levels

synergy_detail.bonus_explanation: This product combines complementary ingredients commonly used together, though clinical synergy data is limited.

clusters.name: Cognitive Performance
clusters.mechanism: Bacopa upregulates tryptophan hydroxylase and serotonin transporter expression, improving synaptic communication. Alpha-GPC provides choline for acetylcholine synthesis. Lion's mane stimulates nerve growth factor (NGF) production. DHA maintains neuronal membrane fluidity critical for synaptic transm
clusters.benefit_short: Bacopa, alpha-GPC, citicoline, and lion's mane support focus and learning — different angles on brain chemistry and nerve growth.

clusters.name: Memory & Learning
clusters.mechanism: Bacopa enhances dendritic branching and synaptic signaling in the hippocampus. Phosphatidylserine maintains neuronal membrane fluidity and supports acetylcholine release. Lion's mane promotes NGF synthesis supporting neuroplasticity. DHA comprises ~40% of polyunsaturated fatty acids in the brain.
clusters.benefit_short: Bacopa, ginkgo, phosphatidylserine, and alpha-GPC support memory and recall — different angles on brain circulation and nerve function.
